correctness.rationale: The exactly specified standard recurrence P0=P1=P2=1 has companion M satisfying M^13=I+3A with integral A. Reducing Pn+1 modulo 3 gives only n=3,4,7 (mod13). The integer backward sequence has P_-9=P_-6=-1, and in both lifted branches the j=1 binomial term is a 3-adic unit times 3(m+1), while j>=2 terms have valuation at least 2+v3(m+1); the n≡3 branch is 3 mod9. The explicit complete residue sets at every valuation level yield densities and sharp per-period extrema (including global 29/13 at N=21,t=1). Independently checked 6,001 integer terms, the M^13 identity and whole periods t=0..6; the proof, not finite checks, covers all t,n.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing shifted prime-two or repdigit Diophantine theorems do not dominate prime-three valuation classes and exact discrepancy bounds. A general 3-adic divisibility framework could in principle cover the result, but none was identified in examined sources.

value.rationale: This classifies the natural integer recurrence at a motivated prime/shift, with two nontrivial 3-adic lifting branches and a sharp uniform discrepancy simultaneously across infinitely many levels. It is more than a periodicity observation or a fixed-length numerical table; exact density and optimal joint counting bound are directly useful for arithmetic distribution questions. No assertion for other primes or shifts.
